message.content: {"caption":"Workflow comparison showing how a shopping agent reaches checkout with and without a reasoning memory.","description":"A two-row workflow diagram compares an online-shopping task. Both rows proceed from left to right, with dotted ellipses marking omitted steps; there are no explicit directional arrows. The upper row, headed “Baseline (No memory),” starts with a miniature shop homepage showing product thumbnails, captioned “Start on homepage.” A red-outlined search stage contains miniature product-listing pages and the red note “Inefficient search for navigation, consuming 8 steps”; its caption says “Cannot filter by ‘Men’, need scroll down.” After an ellipsis is a product-listing screenshot captioned “Select Price 0,” followed by another ellipsis and the action “I will click ‘Proceed to Checkout’ from the cart.” A green check mark accompanies the action, and a dashed box reads “29 Steps in total.” The lower row, headed “Reasoning Bank,” also starts with a shop homepage and product thumbnails, captioned “Start on homepage.” A green-outlined stage shows a product-listing page and is captioned “Hover (Shoes), Hover (Men).” Beneath it, green text reads “According to Memory Item 11, to correctly navigate to certain categories, I need to first filter products ....” The sequence continues to a product-listing screenshot captioned “Select Price 0,” then an ellipsis, then a product-detail screenshot showing a black backpack, captioned “Identified with at least 5 reviews.” It ends with the same “Proceed to Checkout” action and a green check mark, plus a dashed box reading “10 Steps in total.” The diagram contrasts the baseline’s longer search with the memory-guided navigation and fewer total steps.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
